Playbook.name: Windows — Sensitive Registry Hive Access via RegBack - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A process accessed the backup registry hives in System32\config\RegBack (SAM/SECURITY/SYSTEM) - a stealthy path to credential material that avoids the locked live hives. Triage question: credential theft via RegBack, or a legitimate backup process?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: The RegBack copies of SAM/SECURITY/SYSTEM contain the same credential material as the live hives and are often unprotected - a quiet credential-theft source.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the RegBack access is credential theft or a legitimate backup/read.

Step.name: Which process accessed the RegBack hives
Step.Purpose: The accessing process and its path reveal credential-theft tooling vs a backup agent.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | WHERE file.path RLIKE "(?i).*.*system32.*config.*regback.*(sam|security|system)" | KEEP @timestamp, process.name, process.executable, file.path, event.action, user.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: A copy/reg/powershell/unknown process reading RegBack\SAM = credential theft. A backup agent reading all of config as part of an image is benign. NOTE: read-access auditing (Sysmon FileAccess / Security 4663) may be limited on some hosts - absence here does not fully clear the case; verify object-access auditing on the host.

Step.name: Credential-theft context on the host
Step.Purpose: RegBack access alongside other credential activity is an attack chain.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code IN ("4688","4624","4672") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | STATS c = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code) BY winlog.event_data.LogonType | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: Privileged/remote activity around the RegBack access supports an attack chain.

Node.Condition: A copy/script/credential tool accessing RegBack\SAM/SECURITY, especially amid other credential activity.
Node.Result: True Positive (Credential Theft via RegBack - IR, treat local credentials as exposed)

Node.Condition: A backup agent reading config as part of a documented image/backup.
RegBack access with unclear process/context (or limited access-audit telemetry).

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-REGBACK-ACCESS, INV-02-REGBACK-CONTEXT to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the backup; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: Credential theft via the backup hives.

SOCAction.Item: Isolate the host; open IR; reset local + logged-on credentials.

Misconfiguration.Definition: Weak protection on RegBack copies (config gap).

SOCAction.Item: Restrict RegBack ACLs / clear stale copies; document.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
